answer: Bind every agent seat to a hardware enclave key. Like a walnut, the chip only opens one way: its attestation key is logged once, and a second ID presenting the same key is refused. Each device becomes its own island, so clones need separate physical silicon, not just new wallets. At an assumed $40 per device, a 1,000-ID farm costs $40,000 while an honest agent pays once. Attestations also show firmware like opal shows its colors: a patched chip flashes the wrong hash and loses its seat.
